stem.text: Predict before the rule: \(g\) is differentiable for all \(x\) and \(g(2)=-2\). What is true of \(\lim_{x\to2}g(x)\)?

resolution.text: Differentiable at 2 means continuous at 2, so \(\lim_{x\to2}g(x)=g(2)=-2\).

sections.text: A function differentiable at a point is continuous there, and an input outside the domain of \(f\) is outside the domain of \(f'\). The implication runs one way. Contrapositive: not continuous at a point means not differentiable there. Continuity alone supplies nothing about the derivative.
